_README: Aero Balance and the gearing axis, two single-variable changes from the
game's default tune on the GR86. Same car, same parts, same build as
It was taken to attribute the axis shift. It did that for the top ratio,
and it OVERTURNED the aero balance solve published in the previous commit
— see aeroBalanceNotSolved, which is the important part of this file.
screen: tuning menu — GEARING and AERO tabs
baseTune: game default, except where `varied` says otherwise
varied: one item per row — 7th gear ratio, then rear wing

rows.changed: nothing — the default tune, from the sibling fixture
7th ratio restored to 0.85 — the control for row 1

rows.axisNote: NOT READ. The Aero tab does not draw the gearing graph, so this row's axis is missing and it is the one row where it matters most. See axisAttribution.

aeroBalanceNotSolved: THE PREVIOUS COMMIT SAID AERO BALANCE WAS SOLVED AS FRONT DOWNFORCE OVER
TOTAL. THIS ROW KILLS IT.
point 1   F 190, R 232   ->  190/422 = 0.4502    screen 0.45   matches
point 2   F 190, R 290   ->  190/480 = 0.3958    screen 0.42   MISSES
0.024 out, which is five times the rounding window. The model is dead.
HOW IT LOOKED SOLVED ON ONE POINT, because the reasoning error is the
reusable part. 0.4502 against a printed 0.45 read as an exact match to four
decimal places. It was nothing of the kind: AB prints to two decimals, so
anything in [0.445, 0.455] shows as 0.45, and the 'exactness' was an
artefact of comparing a computed number against a rounded one. A 2-dp
readout cannot confirm a model to 4 dp. One point, one coincidence, and a
conclusion that felt earned because the arithmetic was tidy — which is the
same failure as the 3.73 gearing solve and the SPREAD confirmation, three
times in one repository.
WHAT THE TWO POINTS ACTUALLY SUPPORT. Give each end an additive term for
the downforce the bodyshell makes that the wings do not:
AB = (F + a) / (F + a + R + b)
Two equations, two unknowns, so it fits exactly — a is about 175 lb and b
about 215 lb at the printed values. But it fits BY CONSTRUCTION and has no
degrees of freedom left to be tested with, and the rounding window makes
the solution wide: carrying [0.445,0.455] and [0.415,0.425] through gives
a anywhere from roughly 85 to 360 lb. So the SHAPE is supported and the
COEFFICIENTS are not.
CASE A1 PREDICTED THIS AND WAS TALKED OUT OF IT. It says the equal-slider
reading will not be 0.5 'because the body makes downforce the wings do
not'. The previous commit read one point and declared there was no
bodyshell term. There is, and it is large — plausibly comparable to the
wings themselves.
WHAT IS STILL TRUE AND USEFUL: AB is a clean function of the two downforce
numbers in pounds, it responds strongly and monotonically to the wings, and
the app's per-cent-of-range aero output still cannot target it. The A3
floor-and-ceiling readings — each wing at each end, in pounds — now matter
MORE, because they are the four points that pin a and b instead of merely
bracketing a ratio.
axisAttribution: THE TOP GEAR RATIO DOES NOT MOVE THE AXIS. 7th went 0.85 -> 0.75 -> 0.85
and the axis read 159 throughout, with the ratio change plainly visible on
the graph. Candidate 1 from the sibling fixture is eliminated.
THE WING ROW IS MISSING ITS AXIS READING, because the Aero tab does not
draw the gearing graph and the screenshot was taken there. One more shot of
the GEARING tab with the rear wing left at 290 finishes this.
PREDICTION, WRITTEN BEFORE THE READING, because the standing rule is
predictions before readings wherever an ordering is expected:
Aero Efficiency 0.750 (default)        -> axis 159
Aero Efficiency 0.741 (the app's tune) -> axis 157
Aero Efficiency 0.737 (wing at 290)    -> axis 156 or 157
The two known points give roughly 220 axis-mph per unit of aero efficiency;
0.737 sits 0.013 below the default, which is about 2.9 mph, so 156 is the
central estimate and 157 the near miss. Measured top speed moved the same
IF THE AXIS COMES BACK 156 OR 157, E2 IS CLOSED: the axis tracks the car's
drag-limited speed, aero settings move it, the app's tune ran more
downforce than the default, and the 157-versus-159 disagreement was two
correct readings of two different aero setups. IF IT COMES BACK 159, aero
is eliminated too, both candidates are dead, and the cause is something
else in the tune entirely — in which case the next thing to try is a part
change, and a stock GR86 becomes worth buying.
notes: Two oddities recorded without explanation. FIRST: the final drive reads 3.64 in rows 1-3 against the default's 3.63, so it was nudged at some point; it is held constant across those three rows, so the within-batch comparisons stand, but row 0 differs from rows 1-3 by that 0.01 as well as by what `changed` says. SECOND: braking moved with the 7th gear ratio — 60-0 went 63.6 to 63.9 ft with a taller top gear — and 60-0 should not involve 7th at all, since 60 mph is two or three gears down. Either the panel brakes from 60 in whatever gear the car would be in at speed, or something else is going on. It is 0.3 ft, three times the repeat-test spread, so it is not nothing.
